links.outcome: Accuracy of detecting and classifying sensitive health information in medical speech de-identification
links.effect: Top systems reached macro F1 0.7103 and MER 0.1147; average macro F1 was 0.2696 and MER 0.3539. Six fine-tuned models reached F1 0.857-0.867 (precision ~0.885-0.889, recall ~0.830-0.847).
links.quote: The competition attracted 246 teams; top-performing systems achieved a mixed error rate (MER) of 0.1147 and a macro F1-score of 0.7103, with average MER and macro F1-score of 0.3539 and 0.2696, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs for de-identification of sensitive health information in clinical speech transcripts
Community challenge benchmarking of speech transcription and de-identification systems

screen.reason: This study reports on a competitive shared-task benchmark (SREDH/AI-Cup 2025) evaluating speech transcription and sensitive health information de-identification models without evaluating a specific operational deployment practice.
